<explanation>
Based on the file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for MarkUs, which is a web-based application for student assignment submission and grading.

1. Main Components to Include:

a. Client-Side Layer:
   - React components (in app/javascript/Components/)
   - JavaScript assets (in app/assets/javascripts/)
   - Stylesheets (in app/assets/stylesheets/)

b. Server-Side Layer:
   - Rails application (MVC architecture)
   - API controllers (in app/controllers/api/)
   - WebSocket channels (in app/channels/)
   - Background jobs (in app/jobs/)

c. Data Storage Layer:
   - PostgreSQL database (indicated by database.yml.postgresql)
   - Git repositories for student submissions
   - File storage for uploads

d. External Services:
   - LTI integration (Learning Tools Interoperability)
   - Autotest system
   - PDF processing system

2. Architecture Patterns to Highlight:

a. Core Application Structure:
```
[Client Browser] <--> [Nginx/Apache] <--> [Rails App Server]
                                           |
                     [Background Jobs] <--> [Redis]
                           |
                     [PostgreSQL] <--> [Git Storage]
```

b. Key Interactions:
   - Draw arrows showing submission flow
   - Show grading workflow
   - Indicate authentication paths
   - Highlight real-time updates via WebSocket

3. Color Coding Suggestion:

   - Blue: Client-side components
   - Green: Server-side components
   - Yellow: Data storage
   - Orange: External services
   - Purple: Background processing
   - Red: Security components

4. Specific Implementation Details:

a. Authentication & Authorization:
   - Show policy layer (app/policies/)
   - Include LTI authentication flow
   - Role-based access control

b. File Processing:
   - Git repository management
   - PDF annotation system
   - Jupyter notebook handling

c. Assessment Workflow:
   - Assignment submission
   - Automated testing
   - Manual grading
   - Feedback delivery

5. Important Subsystems:

a. Annotation System:
   - Text annotations
   - PDF annotations
   - Image annotations
   - HTML annotations

b. Testing Framework:
   - Test runners
   - Result processing
   - Feedback generation

c. Group Management:
   - Group formation
   - Member management
   - Permission handling

6. Integration Points:

a. External Tools:
   - LTI integration
   - Git interfaces
   - Automated testing services

b. Internal Services:
   - Background job processing
   - WebSocket communication
   - File storage management

7. Deployment Considerations:

a. Container Structure:
   - Show Docker container organization
   - Include service dependencies
   - Highlight scaling points

8. Legend:

Include a comprehensive legend explaining:
   - Component types
   - Arrow meanings
   - Color coding
   - Icon usage
   - State indicators

The diagram should maintain a balance between showing the complex functionality of MarkUs while keeping it clear and understandable. Focus on the major components and their interactions, with the ability to drill down into specific subsystems as needed.

Remember to include version control integration as a key component, as it's central to the application's functionality for handling student submissions. Also emphasize the real-time aspects of the system, such as WebSocket notifications and background job processing.

This architecture should be drawn in a way that emphasizes MarkUs's primary goals: submission management, grading workflow, and feedback delivery, while showing how the technical components work together to achieve these goals.
